graders.name: ranked-report-shape
graders.evidence:
`review-swarm` doesn't exist in this project or the skill list, so I ran the built-in `code-review` skill at high effort on the diff instead. Flask isn't installed here, so I couldn't execute the route, but the findings below come from reading the code and the repo layout.

**Blocking (the endpoint cannot run as committed)**

- **`from app import db` will fail.** There is no `app/__init__.py` and no `db` object defined anywhere in the repo. Importing `app/routes.py` raises ImportError, which takes down the whole module, not just the new route.
- **`Order.query` is a hard-coded `None`** in `app/models.py`, so even with `db` wired up, `Order.query.filter_by(...)` raises AttributeError on every request. The models are placeholders, not ORM-mapped classes.
- **Two Flask app instances.** The route is registered on a fresh `Flask(__name__)` created in `routes.py`, while `db` would be bound to whatever `app/__init__.py` eventually builds. Either the real app never sees the route, or the route hits `db.session` with no bound engine.

**Correctness and security**

- **Unchecked `None` from `.get(order.item_id)`.** If an item is deleted or `item_id` is NULL, `item.name` raises AttributeError and the entire response becomes a 500 rather than returning the user's remaining orders. The zero-orders case you mentioned is actually fine (returns `[]`); the missing-item case is the real crash.
- **No authentication or ownership check.** Any caller can enumerate `/orders/1`, `/orders/2`, ... and read other users' order history. This is an IDOR and should be resolved before the PR, not after.
- **Untyped `user_id` converter.** `/orders/abc` reaches the database as a string comparison against an integer column. Postgres returns a 500; SQLite silently returns an empty 200. Use `<int:user_id>` so Flask returns 404 for non-numeric input.

**Performance and style**

- **N+1 query.** One `Item` lookup per order means a user with 2,000 orders costs 2,001 round-trips. Better: declare `item = relationship(Item)` on `Order` with `selectinload`, or do a single `Item.id.in_(...)` lookup. That also centralizes the None handling at the model layer.
- **`Query.get()` is the deprecated 1.x API.** On SQLAlchemy 2.x it emits a LegacyAPIWarning per request. The current form is `db.session.get(Item, order.item_id)`.

**Tests**

- **No coverage at all.** `tests/test_routes.py` contains only `assert True`, so CI stays green even though the module doesn't import. Beyond the zero-orders test you flagged, add cases for a missing item, a non-numeric user_id, and the import itself.

Suggested order before opening the PR: create `app/__init__.py` with the real app and `db`, replace the model placeholders with mapped classes and an `Order.item` relationship, add an auth check, switch to `<int:user_id>`, then write the tests. I haven't changed any files.

graders.name: ranked-report-shape
graders.evidence:
Review done. One note up front: there is no `review-swarm` skill in this session, so I ran the listed `code-review` skill at high effort with all findings, plus a direct read of the diff, models, and tests.

**Verdict: not ready to open the PR.** The route cannot run at all as written, and two secondary issues would cause 500s once it does.

**Blockers**

- **The import on line 2 fails.** Nothing in the repo defines `db`, and `app/` has no `__init__.py`, so Python treats it as a namespace package with no attributes. Any process that imports `app/routes.py` dies with an ImportError before a route is registered. Fix at the root: add `app/__init__.py` that creates the Flask app and the SQLAlchemy `db`, and move the Flask app construction out of routes to avoid a circular import.
- **The models are placeholders.** In `app/models.py` both `Order.query` and `Item.query` are literally `None`, and neither class defines `id`, `user_id`, `item_id`, or `name`. Even with `db` defined, the first request raises AttributeError on `None.filter_by`. The route needs real `db.Model` subclasses behind it.

**Bugs in the route itself**

- **Missing item crashes the whole list** (line 14). `.get()` returns `None` when an order points at a deleted or NULL item, and `item.name` then raises. One dangling order 500s every order for that user. Guard it or use an outer join.
- **No authorization check** (line 8). Any caller can read any user's orders by changing the path segment. Derive the user from the session or token, or verify ownership.
- **Unconverted `user_id`** (line 8). Use `<int:user_id>` so non-numeric input gets a 404 instead of a database type error on PostgreSQL, and so SQLite does not silently mismatch string vs integer.

**Quality**

- **N+1 queries** (line 13). One `Item` lookup per order. Define an `Order.item` relationship or do a single join. This also removes the None-deref hazard above.
- **Legacy API** (line 13). `Query.get()` warns under SQLAlchemy 2.x. Use `db.session.get(Item, order.item_id)`, and pick one query style instead of mixing `Order.query` with `db.session.query`.

**Tests**

- **Your zero-orders worry is the one case that is actually fine.** An empty result just returns `[]`. The uncovered cases that matter are the import itself, a missing item, and a non-integer id. `tests/test_routes.py` never imports `app.routes`, so the suite stays green while the app cannot start. Add a test-client test for the endpoint covering those three cases.

Flask and SQLAlchemy are not installed in this sandbox, so the import failure was confirmed by inspecting the package layout rather than by running the server.

graders.name: hands-off-to-security-review
graders.evidence:
The right tool for a security-only ask is `/security-review`, and that's what I ran. Its preamble failed because the repo has no `origin` remote, so I did the same single-file review by hand. The middleware is 11 lines, and the findings below are from reading it against known jsonwebtoken behavior. I could not install jsonwebtoken to test empirically because the sandbox denies access to the npm registry, and there is no package.json or node_modules in the repo to tell me which version you depend on.

**Blockers**

- **Missing or empty `JWT_SECRET` is not fail-fast** at `src/middleware/auth.js:6`. On jsonwebtoken 8.5.1 and older, an undefined or empty secret combined with no `algorithms` option makes `verify` accept unsigned `alg: none` tokens, which is a full auth bypass (CVE-2022-23540). On version 9 it instead throws per request, which is safe but means every protected route returns 500. Fix: read the secret once at module load and throw at startup if it is missing, and pin the library to 9.x or newer.
- **No `algorithms` pinned** at `src/middleware/auth.js:6`. The library's defaults are inferred from the secret's shape, so a future switch to a PEM key or an older library version silently changes which algorithms are accepted. Fix: pass `{ algorithms: ['HS256'] }` explicitly.

**Should-fix**

- **Verification errors become 500s with leaked details** at `src/middleware/auth.js:6`. The synchronous `verify` throws on missing, malformed, expired, or bad-signature tokens. Express forwards that to the default error handler, which outside production writes the stack trace and error message to the response. This fails closed, so it is not a bypass, but it discloses internals and lets an attacker distinguish "expired" from "bad signature". Fix: wrap in try/catch and respond 401 with a generic body.
- **No audience or issuer check** at `src/middleware/auth.js:6`. Any token signed with the same secret is accepted as a session, including tokens minted for another purpose or service that shares the secret, such as password-reset or refresh tokens. Fix: set `audience` and `issuer` in the verify options and mint access tokens with matching claims.
- **Tokens without `exp` never expire** at `src/middleware/auth.js:6`. The library only enforces expiry when the claim exists. Fix: pass `maxAge` in verify options, or reject payloads lacking `exp`.
- **Loose scheme parsing** at `src/middleware/auth.js:4-5`. The replace strips the first `Bearer ` anywhere in the string, is case-sensitive, and accepts a raw token with no scheme at all. Not a bypass on its own, but it widens what reaches `verify`. Fix: split on whitespace and require exactly two parts with scheme equal to `bearer` case-insensitively.

**Not an issue**

- Attaching the full payload to `req.user` is fine once the signature is verified. JSON parsing of `__proto__` keys does not pollute the prototype.

**Left out**

- The middleware is not mounted anywhere in `src/app.js` yet, so I could not check which routes it protects or whether any route is reachable without it. Also unverifiable without package.json: the jsonwebtoken version and whether the secret has adequate entropy.
